For quick reference: a hoist is used for anyone who cannot bear weight or transfer independently; a slide sheet is used for in-bed repositioning; a two-person assist is used wherever the MHRA specifies it, never substituted with a single-person technique for convenience; and a ceiling track hoist, where installed, is preferred over a mobile hoist for a person who uses it regularly, reducing set-up time and equipment storage congestion in the room.

Staff with their own physical limitations

A member of staff with their own back condition, pregnancy, or recent injury completes an individual capability assessment with their line manager and, where appropriate, occupational health, resulting in a temporary or ongoing adjustment to which moving and handling tasks they undertake — this is treated the same way as any other reasonable adjustment, discussed openly rather than left for the individual to manage quietly by avoiding certain tasks informally, which risks both their own health and consistent cover for the team.

Continence Care Policy

*Supersedes the version effective 1 May 2025. 'Should' becomes 'must' — the single substantive change: the continence assessment timing and review are no longer merely advisory.*

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how a resident's continence needs are assessed and supported at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every resident at every site.

Policy statement

A continence assessment must be completed within one week of admission and reviewed 6-monthly — no longer merely advisory — supporting a resident's dignity and comfort through an individualised, appropriate approach rather than a one-size-fits-all product or routine.

Definitions

**Continence assessment** the structured assessment of a resident's continence needs, informing their individual care plan, now a mandatory rather than advisory step. **Continence product** the specific product, such as a particular pad type, matched to a resident's assessed needs. **Review point** the 6-monthly point at which the assessment is revisited, or sooner if a resident's needs change, now also mandatory.

Roles and responsibilities

**Care staff** support a resident's continence needs day to day in line with their individual care plan. **A nominated continence lead** at each site completes the initial assessment and the 6-monthly review, both now mandatory obligations rather than expected best practice. **The GP or continence specialist nurse** is involved where the assessment identifies a need beyond what site-level support can address.

Record keeping and retention

Capacity assessments and best interests decisions are retained per the Records Retention Schedule, within the person's care file.

Approval and review history

Appendix: the two-stage test explained

This appendix explains the Act's own two-stage test in more practical detail. Stage one asks whether the person has an impairment or disturbance of the mind or brain, whether permanent or temporary — this alone does not determine incapacity, only whether the second stage needs to be considered at all. Stage two asks whether that impairment means the person cannot, at the time the decision needs to be made, understand relevant information about the decision, retain that information long enough to use it, weigh it up as part of the decision-making process, or communicate their decision by any means. A person lacks capacity for the specific decision only if stage one applies and they fail any one part of stage two — both stages genuinely matter, and staff are trained not to skip from 'has a diagnosis' straight to 'lacks capacity' without properly working through stage two.

Working with family members who hold Lasting Power of Attorney

Where a family member holds a registered Lasting Power of Attorney for health and welfare, or for property and financial affairs, staff confirm the specific scope of that authority before relying on it, since an attorney's authority is decision-specific to the type of LPA registered and does not automatically extend to every decision about the person, and Alderbridge keeps a copy of the registered document on file rather than relying on the family member's own description of their authority.

When a decision genuinely cannot wait

For a decision that must be made urgently and there is no attorney or existing best interests decision in place, the treating professional or care team makes the decision in the person's best interests using the information available at that moment, records the reasoning fully as soon as practicable afterward, and reviews it with fuller information once the urgency has passed, since acting reasonably with incomplete information in a genuine emergency is preferable to delaying necessary care while a more complete process is followed.

Extended worked example: a complaint that reveals a wider issue

A worked example illustrates a complaint acting as an early warning of something more systemic than the individual complainant realised. A family member complains that their relative at Oakfield Lodge seemed unusually drowsy on several recent visits. Purpose and scope

Regular supervision and a meaningful Annual Performance and Development Review give every staff

Video calls and screen sharing while working remotely

During a video call or screen share involving sensitive information, staff confirm no unauthorised person can view or overhear the call, close any unrelated sensitive document before sharing a screen, and use only Alderbridge-approved conferencing tools rather than a personal account on an unapproved platform, applying the same care to a video meeting as to an in-person conversation about the same information.

Wi-Fi security at an approved home location

Home Wi-Fi used for Alderbridge work is secured with a strong, unique password and up-to-date router firmware, and an entirely open or default-password network is not used for any Alderbridge system; where genuinely uncertain about home network security, IT can advise on basic steps to improve it.

Ending a remote working arrangement

Where a remote working arrangement ends, whether by the employee's own request or a genuine business need, IT confirms the issued device and any remote access credential are returned or revoked promptly, following the same access-removal discipline the IT Acceptable Use Policy sets out for a leaver, since a remote arrangement ending is functionally similar to a change of access requirement even where employment itself continues.

Backing up work created while working remotely

Work saved locally on a remote device, rather than directly to an Alderbridge system, is backed up regularly using the approved method IT provides, since a device fault or loss while working remotely should never result in genuinely lost work, and staff are shown how to confirm their own backup is actually running correctly as part of their remote working setup.

Family members and household members during remote work

A family or household member should never have access to an Alderbridge device or account, even briefly and even for an unrelated purpose such as checking their own personal email, since this creates an unnecessary and entirely avoidable risk to data the household member has no reason to see.

Distinguishing a genuine incident from an expected clinical event

Serious Incident Review Policy

Supersedes the version effective 1 May 2025. The review is now chaired by the Chief Executive rather
than the Quality Lead, following a governance restructure.

Trigger

A serious incident review is triggered by any death not from natural causes, a RIDDOR-reportable injury,
or a significant safeguarding failure. The Chief Executive now chairs the review (the Quality Lead
previously did, per the prior version).

Review initiation

A serious incident review begins when harm, credible risk, repeated failure or an external notification
threshold indicates that routine local follow-up is insufficient. The commissioning manager records the
scope, review lead, independence considerations, people to involve and target dates. Immediate safety
action proceeds without waiting for the review, while evidence is preserved proportionately.

Evidence and involvement

The review considers records, chronology, policies, staffing, equipment, decisions and relevant testimony
without treating the first account as conclusive. Residents, representatives and staff are offered an
appropriate opportunity to contribute and are told how their information will be used. The process remains
learning-focused while preserving separate disciplinary, safeguarding or legal routes where those are
required.

Actions and closure

Findings distinguish individual acts, system conditions and uncertainty. Each action has an owner, due
date and measurable completion evidence; an action is not closed merely because a document was
issued. The Quality Lead verifies completion and effectiveness, records any overdue escalation and
communicates the outcome through the correct candour and governance arrangements.

, an investigation is carried out by a manager not otherwise involved, gathering statements and any relevant evidence.

Where the investigation finds a case to answer, the employee is invited in writing to a formal hearing, given at least 2 working days' notice, told the specific allegation, and provided with the investigation evidence in advance.

The employee has the right to be accompanied at the hearing by a trade union representative or a work colleague of their choice.

At the hearing, the employee is given a full opportunity to respond to the allegation, ask questions, and present their own evidence before any decision is reached.

A decision is confirmed in writing within 5 working days of the hearing wherever possible, giving reasons and, where a sanction is applied, its duration and the right of appeal.

The first formal stage is normally a first written warning, live for 6 months; a further offence within that period, or a sufficiently serious first offence, may move directly to a final written warning, live for 12 months.

A further offence while a final written warning is live may result in dismissal with notice, or without notice if the conduct amounts to gross misconduct.

An employee may appeal any formal outcome in writing within 10 working days, to a manager not previously involved, whose decision is final within Alderbridge's own internal process.

Gross misconduct examples

Examples of gross misconduct include theft, physical violence, being under the influence of drugs or alcohol on duty, gross negligence causing serious harm to a person supported, serious breach of the Safe Administration of Medication Policy or Controlled Drugs Procedure, and serious or repeated breach of confidentiality. This is not an exhaustive list; the Employee Handbook's Section 4 gives further illustrative examples, and a matter not listed here may still be treated as gross misconduct where its seriousness genuinely warrants it.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where an allegation also raises a safeguarding concern, the Safeguarding Adults Policy and Allegations Against Staff Procedure run in parallel with this procedure; a decision to suspend on full pay pending investigation is taken on safeguarding grounds and is never treated as itself a disciplinary sanction or a presumption of guilt.

Local and regional variations

No local or regional variation applies to this procedure — disciplinary process is deliberately standardised across all five sites and Central Support Office to ensure consistent, fair treatment regardless of location.

Allegations Against Staff Procedure

Supersedes the version effective 1 January 2024. Shortens the LADO referral window from one working

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group responds when an allegation is made against a
member of staff that they have harmed, or placed at risk of harm, a resident. It applies to every site and
every category of staff, including agency and bank workers.

Policy statement

Every allegation against a member of staff is taken seriously, investigated fairly and reported through the
correct external channels, protecting both residents and the staff member's own right to a fair process
while the allegation is looked into.

Definitions

**Allegation** a concern that a staff member has behaved in a way that has harmed or may harm a
resident, whether reported by a resident, a family member, a colleague, or observed directly. **LADO** the
Local Authority Designated Officer, the external role responsible for overseeing how an organisation
manages an allegation against a person working with adults at risk. **Precautionary suspension** a
temporary removal of a staff member from duty while an allegation is investigated, which is not itself a
disciplinary finding.

Roles and responsibilities

**Any member of staff** who becomes aware of an allegation reports it immediately to the registered
manager, never investigating or confronting the accused staff member themselves. **The registered
manager** makes the initial referral decision and contacts the LADO the same working day. **The
Alderbridge Safeguarding Lead** oversees the internal investigation alongside any external process, and
now also provides the documented second opinion on any decision not to suspend.

1. Report any allegation to the registered manager immediately; do not investigate, confront the accused
staff member, or delay reporting to gather further evidence first.

For quick reference: identify hazards; identify who might be harmed; evaluate existing controls and residual risk; identify further action needed; record, communicate and review.

Assessing risk for a person with fluctuating needs

Where a person's needs fluctuate significantly (for example, a condition with good and bad days), the risk assessment records the range of presentation rather than a single snapshot, and staff are trained to recognise which end of that range they are seeing on a given day so the correct control measure is applied at the right time rather than a single fixed approach being used regardless of how the person actually presents that day.

Risk assessment for one-off events and visits

A one-off event (a fundraising open day, an external visit) receives its own proportionate risk assessment covering the event's specific hazards, completed with enough lead time to put any necessary control in place, rather than being run under a standing, unrelated risk assessment that does not actually address what is different about the event.

When a risk assessment reveals a risk that cannot be adequately controlled

Where an assessment finds a risk that cannot be reduced to an acceptable level with any available control, the activity does not proceed in that form; the registered manager and, where relevant, the Health and Safety Lead consider whether the activity can be modified to remove the unacceptable element, or whether it should not proceed at all, rather than proceeding regardless because stopping the activity feels operationally inconvenient.

Purpose and scope

This procedure sets out how Alderbridge Care Group checks a new starter's right to work in the UK. It applies to every new starter at every site.

Policy statement

HR must check right-to-work documents before a new starter's first day — no employee may start work without this check having been completed and recorded — meeting Alderbridge's legal obligation to confirm every employee is legally entitled to work before they begin.

Definitions

**Right-to-work check** the document check confirming a person's legal entitlement to work in the UK, following the current Home Office guidance on acceptable document types, now a mandatory precondition to starting work rather than an expected best practice. **Document retention copy** the copy of the checked document retained as evidence the check was completed correctly.

Roles and responsibilities

**HR** must complete the right-to-work check before a new starter's first day and retain the document copy; this is now a mandatory precondition, not merely expected practice. **The registered manager** confirms with HR that a check is complete before allowing a new starter to begin their first shift, and must not permit a start without this confirmation. **The new starter** provides the required original document promptly when asked.

1. Request the required right-to-work document from a new starter as soon as an offer is accepted, allowing time to complete the mandatory check before their first day.
2. Check the original document in person, or via the Home Office's online right-to-work checking service where applicable, following current guidance on acceptable evidence.
3. Retain a copy of the checked document, dated and annotated to confirm when and how the check was completed.
4. No employee may start work without this check having been completed and recorded; this is now an absolute requirement, a tightening from the previous version's advisory wording.

Learning from Deaths Policy

*Supersedes the version effective 1 February 2025. Sections reordered to lead with family communication before the review process; no requirement changed.*

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group communicates with a resident's family following their death, and how the death is reviewed to identify any genuine learning. It applies to every site.

Policy statement

Every family is thanked for their trust and invited to share feedback on the care provided, and every death is briefly reviewed at the next Quality Committee to identify any learning, without implying any death was unexpected or poorly managed.

Definitions

**Learning from deaths review** the brief, routine review conducted for every resident death, distinct from a fuller investigation triggered by a specific concern. **Quality Committee** the body that receives the review and any theme identified across multiple reviews over time.

Roles and responsibilities

**A nominated staff member** contacts the family sensitively to thank them and, where appropriate, invite feedback. **The registered manager** prepares a brief summary for the Quality Committee following every death. **The Quality Committee** identifies any genuine, recurring learning theme across reviews.

1. Contact the family, at a sensitive and appropriate time, to thank them for their trust in Alderbridge's care.
2. Invite the family to share feedback on the care provided, where this feels appropriate given their circumstances, without pressuring them to respond.
3. Prepare a brief review summary for every resident death, presented at the next Quality Committee meeting.
4. Identify whether the review suggests any genuine learning, distinct from the routine, expected nature of end of life care generally.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Where a death raises a specific concern beyond the routine review (for example, an unexpected circumstance), this is escalated to a fuller investigation under the Incident Reporting Policy and, where relevant, the Duty of Candour Guidance, rather than being addressed only through the routine Quality Committee review.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how catering and menu planning works at Alderbridge Care Group. It applies to every site's kitchen and catering team.

Policy statement

Each site runs a four-week menu that rotates on a fixed cycle. Residents are consulted on the menu twice a year, and every resident's dietary and allergen needs are recorded individually, balancing variety and choice with the practical needs of a catering operation serving many residents.

Definitions

**Four-week rotating menu** the fixed cycle of menus that repeats every four weeks, providing variety without requiring an entirely new menu created constantly. **Dietary requirement** a resident's specific need, such as a texture-modified diet or a cultural or religious dietary preference. **Allergen record** the record of a resident's known allergen, checked against every meal prepared for them.

Roles and responsibilities

**The catering team** prepares meals in line with the current menu and each resident's individual dietary and allergen record. **The registered manager** ensures residents are consulted ahead of each twice-yearly menu review. **A nominated staff member** keeps the allergen record for every resident current and clearly communicated to the kitchen.

1. Follow the current four-week rotating menu, preparing meals consistent with what is published for each day.
2. Record every resident's dietary requirement and known allergen individually, checked against every meal prepared for them.
3. Consult residents twice a year, incorporating genuine preference into the next menu cycle where practicable.
4. Update a resident's dietary or allergen record immediately if their needs change, communicating this to the kitchen the same day.

What a formal absence review meeting actually covers

A formal absence review meeting triggered at the red level is a genuinely two-way conversation, not a predetermined disciplinary step: it reviews the specific pattern openly, explores whether an underlying cause (health, workplace factors, or personal circumstances) can be identified and addressed, considers whether occupational health input would help, and only where a pattern is not disability-related and shows no sign of improving despite support does it begin to move toward considering whether continued employment in the current role remains sustainable — a possibility discussed transparently rather than left unspoken while informally already decided.

Confidentiality of health information disclosed during absence management

Any health information an employee shares as part of a return-to-work discussion or a formal absence review is treated as confidential, shared only with those who genuinely need to know (for example, HR and, where a reasonable adjustment is agreed, the employee's own line manager) rather than discussed more widely, and an employee is never expected to disclose more clinical detail than they are comfortable sharing beyond what a fit note or occupational health report already confirms.

Absence during a probationary period

A probationary employee's absence is monitored against the same trigger points, but the shorter probationary window means HR and the line manager review any absence pattern more promptly, since a genuine, sustained concern about attendance reliability is relevant to the eventual probation confirmation decision under the Probationary Period Policy, discussed openly with the employee rather than left unaddressed until the probation end date arrives.

Closing note on tone

Every conversation this policy describes — a return-to-work discussion, an absence review, a trigger-point escalation — is expected to be conducted with genuine warmth and curiosity about what is actually going on for the employee, since a policy applied correctly but coldly achieves compliance without achieving the actual purpose this policy exists for, which is a workplace where people feel able to be honest about being unwell and supported back when they are ready.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group provides regular supervision and an Annual Performance
and Development Review for every member of staff. It applies to every site and every category of
permanent staff.

Policy statement

Regular supervision and a meaningful Annual Performance and Development Review give every staff
member a structured opportunity to reflect on their practice, raise a concern, and plan their own
development, supporting both individual growth and the quality of care residents receive.

Definitions

**Supervision** a regular one-to-one meeting between a staff member and their line manager, focused on
current practice and immediate support needs. **Annual Performance and Development Review** the
renamed term for what the previous version called an appraisal — the annual, more formal review of a
staff member's overall performance over the past year and their development plan for the year ahead.
**Personal development plan** the agreed set of development actions arising from the Annual
Performance and Development Review.

Roles and responsibilities

**Line managers** conduct supervision at least monthly for every direct report and lead the Annual
Performance and Development Review. **HR** monitors that supervision and the Annual Performance
and Development Review are completed on schedule across all sites. **Staff** come prepared to raise
their own topics in supervision and the review, not only respond to what their manager raises.

1. Conduct supervision with every direct report at least monthly, recorded briefly to note any action agreed.

2. Complete an Annual Performance and Development Review for every staff member annually, covering
performance over the year and a personal development plan for the year ahead; this is the same annual
process previously called an appraisal, renamed in this version.

Conduct at social events and outside work

Where staff attend an Alderbridge-organised social event, the same fundamental standards of respect and appropriate behaviour apply, though the specific dress code and formality of the workplace itself is relaxed; conduct that would be a disciplinary matter at work (harassment, discrimination) remains exactly as serious at a work social event, since the change of setting does not change the underlying standard expected.

Personal relationships between colleagues

A personal relationship between two colleagues is not itself prohibited, but where one holds a direct managerial or supervisory relationship over the other, this is disclosed to HR so that any potential conflict of interest — for example, in a performance review, a shift allocation decision, or a disciplinary matter — can be managed transparently, protecting both individuals and the fairness of the process for everyone else involved.

Conduct expectations around confidentiality of care information

Beyond the general confidentiality expectation stated earlier, staff are specifically reminded that information about a person supported's health, behaviour or personal circumstances is shared only on a genuine need-to-know basis even within the team, since casual staff-room discussion of a resident's private affairs is a real and recurring risk this section is written to explicitly discourage, not merely a theoretical concern.

Conduct towards contractors and external professionals

Staff extend the same courtesy and professionalism to contractors, visiting healthcare professionals and inspectors as to colleagues and residents, recognising that these interactions also shape how Alderbridge is perceived externally and that a defensive or unhelpful attitude toward, for example, a CQC inspector reflects poorly on the whole organisation regardless of any individual's personal view of a specific visit.

Use of alcohol and substances

Staff do not attend work under the influence of alcohol or any substance affecting their ability to work safely, and any such concern is raised with the registered manager immediately given the direct safety implications in a care environment; occasional moderate alcohol consumption at an evening work social event, where staff are not on duty or on call, is a separate matter handled with ordinary common sense.

Probationary Period Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out the probationary period every new employee serves, and how it is reviewed and confirmed. It applies to every new starter, and to any existing employee moving into a new role that Alderbridge treats as requiring a fresh probationary assessment.

Policy statement

Probation is a genuine, two-way assessment period: Alderbridge assesses whether the new starter is settling well and meeting the role's requirements, and the new starter assesses whether the role and Alderbridge are right for them, with support and honest feedback flowing in both directions throughout.

Definitions

**Probationary period** the standard 6-month period from an employee's start date during which suitability is formally assessed. **Extension** an additional period, up to 3 months, added where more time is genuinely needed to reach a fair decision. **Probation review** a scheduled formal conversation reviewing progress against the role's requirements.

Roles and responsibilities

**The line manager** holds regular informal check-ins and every formal review, raising any concern as soon as it arises rather than saving it for a scheduled review. **HR** confirms the outcome of each formal review in writing and advises on any complex case. **The new starter** engages openly with feedback and raises any concern about their own induction or support.

The probationary period runs for 6 months from the start date, extendable by up to a further 3 months at the registered manager's discretion where more time is needed.

Formal review meetings are held at 6 weeks, 3 months and 5 months, each recorded in writing.

Any conduct, capability or attendance concern is raised with the employee as soon as it arises, not held back until the next scheduled review.

Successful completion of probation is confirmed to the employee in writing, normally by the end of the 6-month period.

What a formal absence review meeting actually covers

A formal absence review meeting triggered at the red level is a genuinely two-way conversation, not a predetermined disciplinary step: it reviews the specific pattern openly, explores whether an underlying cause (health, workplace factors, or personal circumstances) can be identified and addressed, considers whether occupational health input would help, and only where a pattern is not disability-related and shows no sign of improving despite support does it begin to move toward considering whether continued employment in the current role remains sustainable — a possibility discussed transparently rather than left unspoken while informally already decided.

Confidentiality of health information disclosed during absence management

Any health information an employee shares as part of a return-to-work discussion or a formal absence review is treated as confidential, shared only with those who genuinely need to know (for example, HR and, where a reasonable adjustment is agreed, the employee's own line manager) rather than discussed more widely, and an employee is never expected to disclose more clinical detail than they are comfortable sharing beyond what a fit note or occupational health report already confirms.

Absence during a probationary period

A probationary employee's absence is monitored against the same trigger points, but the shorter probationary window means HR and the line manager review any absence pattern more promptly, since a genuine, sustained concern about attendance reliability is relevant to the eventual probation confirmation decision under the Probationary Period Policy, discussed openly with the employee rather than left unaddressed until the probation end date arrives.

Closing note on tone

Every conversation this policy describes — a return-to-work discussion, an absence review, a trigger-point escalation — is expected to be conducted with genuine warmth and curiosity about what is actually going on for the employee, since a policy applied correctly but coldly achieves compliance without achieving the actual purpose this policy exists for, which is a workplace where people feel able to be honest about being unwell and supported back when they are ready.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group provides regular supervision and an Annual Performance
and Development Review for every member of staff. It applies to every site and every category of
permanent staff.

Policy statement

Regular supervision and a meaningful Annual Performance and Development Review give every staff
member a structured opportunity to reflect on their practice, raise a concern, and plan their own
development, supporting both individual growth and the quality of care residents receive.

Definitions

**Supervision** a regular one-to-one meeting between a staff member and their line manager, focused on
current practice and immediate support needs. **Annual Performance and Development Review** the
renamed term for what the previous version called an appraisal — the annual, more formal review of a
staff member's overall performance over the past year and their development plan for the year ahead.
**Personal development plan** the agreed set of development actions arising from the Annual
Performance and Development Review.

Roles and responsibilities

**Line managers** conduct supervision at least monthly for every direct report and lead the Annual
Performance and Development Review. **HR** monitors that supervision and the Annual Performance
and Development Review are completed on schedule across all sites. **Staff** come prepared to raise
their own topics in supervision and the review, not only respond to what their manager raises.

1. Conduct supervision with every direct report at least monthly, recorded briefly to note any action agreed.

2. Complete an Annual Performance and Development Review for every staff member annually, covering
performance over the year and a personal development plan for the year ahead; this is the same annual
process previously called an appraisal, renamed in this version.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Absence wholly attributable to a disability within the meaning of the Equality Act 2010, or to pregnancy-related illness occurring in the two weeks following childbirth, is disregarded when calculating whether a trigger point has been reached, reflecting Alderbridge's legal obligation not to treat a disability-related absence the same as an unrelated one for this purpose. Where it is genuinely unclear whether an absence qualifies for this treatment, HR makes the assessment based on medical evidence, in consultation with occupational health where needed, rather than the line manager deciding informally.

Local and regional variations

No local or regional variation applies to the reporting timescale or trigger points themselves, which are deliberately standardised; what does vary by site is the specific staffing-cover arrangement a registered manager puts in place for a given absence, since a Willow Bank community visit gap is covered differently in practice from a residential shift gap, even though the underlying reporting and review process is identical.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Annual Leave Policy (an absence recorded as sickness is never quietly reclassified as annual leave, or vice versa, regardless of staffing pressure), the Disciplinary Procedure (used only where absence itself, rather than the underlying health condition, becomes a conduct matter — for example, a pattern of unauthorised absence with no genuine health explanation), and the Probationary Period Policy (a probationary employee's absence is reviewed against the same trigger points, though the shorter probationary timeframe means a pattern may become apparent, and relevant to a probation decision, more quickly).

Conduct at social events and outside work

Where staff attend an Alderbridge-organised social event, the same fundamental standards of respect and appropriate behaviour apply, though the specific dress code and formality of the workplace itself is relaxed; conduct that would be a disciplinary matter at work (harassment, discrimination) remains exactly as serious at a work social event, since the change of setting does not change the underlying standard expected.

Personal relationships between colleagues

A personal relationship between two colleagues is not itself prohibited, but where one holds a direct managerial or supervisory relationship over the other, this is disclosed to HR so that any potential conflict of interest — for example, in a performance review, a shift allocation decision, or a disciplinary matter — can be managed transparently, protecting both individuals and the fairness of the process for everyone else involved.

Conduct expectations around confidentiality of care information

Beyond the general confidentiality expectation stated earlier, staff are specifically reminded that information about a person supported's health, behaviour or personal circumstances is shared only on a genuine need-to-know basis even within the team, since casual staff-room discussion of a resident's private affairs is a real and recurring risk this section is written to explicitly discourage, not merely a theoretical concern.

Conduct towards contractors and external professionals

Staff extend the same courtesy and professionalism to contractors, visiting healthcare professionals and inspectors as to colleagues and residents, recognising that these interactions also shape how Alderbridge is perceived externally and that a defensive or unhelpful attitude toward, for example, a CQC inspector reflects poorly on the whole organisation regardless of any individual's personal view of a specific visit.

Use of alcohol and substances

Staff do not attend work under the influence of alcohol or any substance affecting their ability to work safely, and any such concern is raised with the registered manager immediately given the direct safety implications in a care environment; occasional moderate alcohol consumption at an evening work social event, where staff are not on duty or on call, is a separate matter handled with ordinary common sense.

Reviewing an ongoing flexible arrangement

An established flexible working arrangement is reviewed periodically by mutual agreement, particularly
following a significant change in the role or the site's own staffing model, to confirm it continues to work
well for both the employee and the team, rather than being fixed permanently from the point of approval
with no further conversation.

Final note

Flexibility and reliable, safe staffing are not opposites at Alderbridge; this policy exists precisely because
well-designed flexible working, properly supported, tends to improve retention and therefore staffing
reliability over time, not undermine it.

Requests for a temporary rather than permanent change

An employee may request a flexible working change for a defined temporary period (for example, during a
period of caring responsibility) rather than permanently; this is discussed and agreed on the same basis as
a permanent request, with a clear, mutually understood end date or review point recorded at the outset.

Supporting a manager new to handling flexible working requests

A manager considering their first flexible working request is paired with an HR adviser for that first case,
walking through the statutory timescale, the permitted business reasons for refusal, and how to structure a
fair, well-documented decision, so the manager's own confidence and consistency builds through direct
support rather than relying solely on written policy guidance for a genuinely new and sometimes finely
balanced type of decision to make alone.

Closing note

Flexible working, handled well, is one of the clearest practical demonstrations of Alderbridge trusting its
own staff as adults capable of managing their own working lives responsibly, and every manager applying
this policy is asked to keep that underlying spirit in mind alongside its specific procedural steps.

Probationary Period Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out the probationary period every new employee serves, and how it is reviewed and confirmed. It applies to every new starter, and to any existing employee moving into a new role that Alderbridge treats as requiring a fresh probationary assessment.

Policy statement

Probation is a genuine, two-way assessment period: Alderbridge assesses whether the new starter is settling well and meeting the role's requirements, and the new starter assesses whether the role and Alderbridge are right for them, with support and honest feedback flowing in both directions throughout.

Definitions

**Probationary period** the standard 6-month period from an employee's start date during which suitability is formally assessed. **Extension** an additional period, up to 3 months, added where more time is genuinely needed to reach a fair decision. **Probation review** a scheduled formal conversation reviewing progress against the role's requirements.

Roles and responsibilities

**The line manager** holds regular informal check-ins and every formal review, raising any concern as soon as it arises rather than saving it for a scheduled review. **HR** confirms the outcome of each formal review in writing and advises on any complex case. **The new starter** engages openly with feedback and raises any concern about their own induction or support.

The probationary period runs for 6 months from the start date, extendable by up to a further 3 months at the registered manager's discretion where more time is needed.

Formal review meetings are held at 6 weeks, 3 months and 5 months, each recorded in writing.

Any conduct, capability or attendance concern is raised with the employee as soon as it arises, not held back until the next scheduled review.

Successful completion of probation is confirmed to the employee in writing, normally by the end of the 6-month period.

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out how Alderbridge Care Group provides regular supervision and an Annual Performance
and Development Review for every member of staff. It applies to every site and every category of
permanent staff.

Policy statement

Regular supervision and a meaningful Annual Performance and Development Review give every staff
member a structured opportunity to reflect on their practice, raise a concern, and plan their own
development, supporting both individual growth and the quality of care residents receive.

Definitions

**Supervision** a regular one-to-one meeting between a staff member and their line manager, focused on
current practice and immediate support needs. **Annual Performance and Development Review** the
renamed term for what the previous version called an appraisal — the annual, more formal review of a
staff member's overall performance over the past year and their development plan for the year ahead.
**Personal development plan** the agreed set of development actions arising from the Annual
Performance and Development Review.

Roles and responsibilities

**Line managers** conduct supervision at least monthly for every direct report and lead the Annual
Performance and Development Review. **HR** monitors that supervision and the Annual Performance
and Development Review are completed on schedule across all sites. **Staff** come prepared to raise
their own topics in supervision and the review, not only respond to what their manager raises.

1. Conduct supervision with every direct report at least monthly, recorded briefly to note any action agreed.

2. Complete an Annual Performance and Development Review for every staff member annually, covering
performance over the year and a personal development plan for the year ahead; this is the same annual
process previously called an appraisal, renamed in this version.

Exceptions and professional judgement

Absence wholly attributable to a disability within the meaning of the Equality Act 2010, or to pregnancy-related illness occurring in the two weeks following childbirth, is disregarded when calculating whether a trigger point has been reached, reflecting Alderbridge's legal obligation not to treat a disability-related absence the same as an unrelated one for this purpose. Where it is genuinely unclear whether an absence qualifies for this treatment, HR makes the assessment based on medical evidence, in consultation with occupational health where needed, rather than the line manager deciding informally.

Local and regional variations

No local or regional variation applies to the reporting timescale or trigger points themselves, which are deliberately standardised; what does vary by site is the specific staffing-cover arrangement a registered manager puts in place for a given absence, since a Willow Bank community visit gap is covered differently in practice from a residential shift gap, even though the underlying reporting and review process is identical.

Interaction with other Alderbridge policies

This policy works alongside the Annual Leave Policy (an absence recorded as sickness is never quietly reclassified as annual leave, or vice versa, regardless of staffing pressure), the Disciplinary Procedure (used only where absence itself, rather than the underlying health condition, becomes a conduct matter — for example, a pattern of unauthorised absence with no genuine health explanation), and the Probationary Period Policy (a probationary employee's absence is reviewed against the same trigger points, though the shorter probationary timeframe means a pattern may become apparent, and relevant to a probation decision, more quickly).

Conduct at social events and outside work

Where staff attend an Alderbridge-organised social event, the same fundamental standards of respect and appropriate behaviour apply, though the specific dress code and formality of the workplace itself is relaxed; conduct that would be a disciplinary matter at work (harassment, discrimination) remains exactly as serious at a work social event, since the change of setting does not change the underlying standard expected.

Personal relationships between colleagues

A personal relationship between two colleagues is not itself prohibited, but where one holds a direct managerial or supervisory relationship over the other, this is disclosed to HR so that any potential conflict of interest — for example, in a performance review, a shift allocation decision, or a disciplinary matter — can be managed transparently, protecting both individuals and the fairness of the process for everyone else involved.

Conduct expectations around confidentiality of care information

Beyond the general confidentiality expectation stated earlier, staff are specifically reminded that information about a person supported's health, behaviour or personal circumstances is shared only on a genuine need-to-know basis even within the team, since casual staff-room discussion of a resident's private affairs is a real and recurring risk this section is written to explicitly discourage, not merely a theoretical concern.

Conduct towards contractors and external professionals

Staff extend the same courtesy and professionalism to contractors, visiting healthcare professionals and inspectors as to colleagues and residents, recognising that these interactions also shape how Alderbridge is perceived externally and that a defensive or unhelpful attitude toward, for example, a CQC inspector reflects poorly on the whole organisation regardless of any individual's personal view of a specific visit.

Use of alcohol and substances

Staff do not attend work under the influence of alcohol or any substance affecting their ability to work safely, and any such concern is raised with the registered manager immediately given the direct safety implications in a care environment; occasional moderate alcohol consumption at an evening work social event, where staff are not on duty or on call, is a separate matter handled with ordinary common sense.

Reviewing an ongoing flexible arrangement

An established flexible working arrangement is reviewed periodically by mutual agreement, particularly
following a significant change in the role or the site's own staffing model, to confirm it continues to work
well for both the employee and the team, rather than being fixed permanently from the point of approval
with no further conversation.

Final note

Flexibility and reliable, safe staffing are not opposites at Alderbridge; this policy exists precisely because
well-designed flexible working, properly supported, tends to improve retention and therefore staffing
reliability over time, not undermine it.

Requests for a temporary rather than permanent change

An employee may request a flexible working change for a defined temporary period (for example, during a
period of caring responsibility) rather than permanently; this is discussed and agreed on the same basis as
a permanent request, with a clear, mutually understood end date or review point recorded at the outset.

Supporting a manager new to handling flexible working requests

A manager considering their first flexible working request is paired with an HR adviser for that first case,
walking through the statutory timescale, the permitted business reasons for refusal, and how to structure a
fair, well-documented decision, so the manager's own confidence and consistency builds through direct
support rather than relying solely on written policy guidance for a genuinely new and sometimes finely
balanced type of decision to make alone.

Closing note

Flexible working, handled well, is one of the clearest practical demonstrations of Alderbridge trusting its
own staff as adults capable of managing their own working lives responsibly, and every manager applying
this policy is asked to keep that underlying spirit in mind alongside its specific procedural steps.

Probationary Period Policy

Purpose and scope

This policy sets out the probationary period every new employee serves, and how it is reviewed and confirmed. It applies to every new starter, and to any existing employee moving into a new role that Alderbridge treats as requiring a fresh probationary assessment.

Policy statement

Probation is a genuine, two-way assessment period: Alderbridge assesses whether the new starter is settling well and meeting the role's requirements, and the new starter assesses whether the role and Alderbridge are right for them, with support and honest feedback flowing in both directions throughout.

Definitions

**Probationary period** the standard 6-month period from an employee's start date during which suitability is formally assessed. **Extension** an additional period, up to 3 months, added where more time is genuinely needed to reach a fair decision. **Probation review** a scheduled formal conversation reviewing progress against the role's requirements.

Roles and responsibilities

**The line manager** holds regular informal check-ins and every formal review, raising any concern as soon as it arises rather than saving it for a scheduled review. **HR** confirms the outcome of each formal review in writing and advises on any complex case. **The new starter** engages openly with feedback and raises any concern about their own induction or support.

The probationary period runs for 6 months from the start date, extendable by up to a further 3 months at the registered manager's discretion where more time is needed.

Formal review meetings are held at 6 weeks, 3 months and 5 months, each recorded in writing.

Any conduct, capability or attendance concern is raised with the employee as soon as it arises, not held back until the next scheduled review.

Successful completion of probation is confirmed to the employee in writing, normally by the end of the 6-month period.

How the wellbeing and benefits summary is kept current

Keeping this handbook up to date

Worked example

A new care assistant starts in March, receiving the increased £55 initial allowance in their first month's pay to purchase their starting uniform, £15 more than the previous version provided; the following April, they receive the increased £35 replacement allowance alongside every other uniformed staff member.

manually excluded, and every occasion within the current rolling window counts regardless of whether it happened at the very start or the very end of that window; this rolling approach is explained to every employee at induction, since a fixed calendar-year approach would otherwise create an artificial reset each January that does not reflect the underlying pattern being monitored.

What a formal absence review meeting actually covers

A formal absence review meeting triggered at the red level is a genuinely two-way conversation, not a predetermined disciplinary step: it reviews the specific pattern openly, explores whether an underlying cause (health, workplace factors, or personal circumstances) can be identified and addressed, considers whether occupational health input would help, and only where a pattern is not disability-related and shows no sign of improving despite support does it begin to move toward considering whether continued employment in the current role remains sustainable — a possibility discussed transparently rather than left unspoken while informally already decided.

Confidentiality of health information disclosed during absence management

Any health information an employee shares as part of a return-to-work discussion or a formal absence review is treated as confidential, shared only with those who genuinely need to know (for example, HR and, where a reasonable adjustment is agreed, the employee's own line manager) rather than discussed more widely, and an employee is never expected to disclose more clinical detail than they are comfortable sharing beyond what a fit note or occupational health report already confirms.

Absence during a probationary period

A probationary employee's absence is monitored against the same trigger points, but the shorter probationary window means HR and the line manager review any absence pattern more promptly, since a genuine, sustained concern about attendance reliability is relevant to the eventual probation confirmation decision under the Probationary Period Policy, discussed openly with the employee rather than left unaddressed until the probation end date arrives.

Closing note on tone

Every conversation this policy describes — a return-to-work discussion, an absence review, a trigger-point escalation — is expected to be conducted with genuine warmth and curiosity about what is actually going on for the employee, since a policy applied correctly but coldly achieves compliance without achieving the actual purpose this policy exists for, which is a workplace where people feel able to be honest about being unwell and supported back when they are ready.

Linking the review to career progression

Where a staff member expresses interest in progressing to a more senior role, this is discussed as part of
the Annual Performance and Development Review and reflected in the personal development plan,
identifying the specific training or experience that would support that progression rather than leaving the
ambition undiscussed until a vacancy happens to arise.

New manager induction into supervision practice

A newly promoted line manager receives additional coaching on conducting supervision well before taking
on this responsibility for the first time, since giving good supervision is itself a skill that benefits from
support rather than being assumed to come automatically with a management title.

Supervision for an agency or bank worker

A regular agency or bank worker who covers shifts consistently at a site is also offered a lighter-touch
supervision conversation periodically with the shift lead, distinct from the more formal Alderbridge
employment relationship they have with their own agency, since a worker who is a familiar, regular
presence still benefits from the same kind of reflective conversation as a permanent colleague.

Group supervision alongside one-to-one sessions

Some sites also hold an occasional group supervision session covering a shared practice theme relevant
to the whole team, such as a recent change in a care approach, which complements but never replaces
the individual one-to-one supervision each staff member is separately entitled to.

Confidentiality of supervision content

What is discussed in supervision is treated as confidential between the staff member and their line
manager, save where it raises a safeguarding, conduct or safety concern that must be escalated under the
relevant separate policy, and staff are told clearly at the outset where that boundary sits so they can speak
openly within it.

Policy statement

Definitions

Policy statement

What a formal absence review meeting actually covers

A formal absence review meeting triggered at the red level is a genuinely two-way conversation, not a predetermined disciplinary step: it reviews the specific pattern openly, explores whether an underlying cause (health, workplace factors, or personal circumstances) can be identified and addressed, considers whether occupational health input would help, and only where a pattern is not disability-related and shows no sign of improving despite support does it begin to move toward considering whether continued employment in the current role remains sustainable — a possibility discussed transparently rather than left unspoken while informally already decided.

Confidentiality of health information disclosed during absence management

Any health information an employee shares as part of a return-to-work discussion or a formal absence review is treated as confidential, shared only with those who genuinely need to know (for example, HR and, where a reasonable adjustment is agreed, the employee's own line manager) rather than discussed more widely, and an employee is never expected to disclose more clinical detail than they are comfortable sharing beyond what a fit note or occupational health report already confirms.

Absence during a probationary period

A probationary employee's absence is monitored against the same trigger points, but the shorter probationary window means HR and the line manager review any absence pattern more promptly, since a genuine, sustained concern about attendance reliability is relevant to the eventual probation confirmation decision under the Probationary Period Policy, discussed openly with the employee rather than left unaddressed until the probation end date arrives.

Closing note on tone

Every conversation this policy describes — a return-to-work discussion, an absence review, a trigger-point escalation — is expected to be conducted with genuine warmth and curiosity about what is actually going on for the employee, since a policy applied correctly but coldly achieves compliance without achieving the actual purpose this policy exists for, which is a workplace where people feel able to be honest about being unwell and supported back when they are ready.

How the wellbeing and benefits summary is kept current

Keeping this handbook up to date

This handbook is reviewed at least annually, and sooner where a significant change to an underlying policy makes an earlier update worthwhile, such as the wellbeing and benefits consolidation reflected in this version; a change is communicated to staff through the usual internal communication channels.

Feedback on this handbook

An employee is welcome to suggest an improvement to this handbook, such as a topic that feels missing or a section that reads unclearly, through their registered manager or directly to Human Resources; a handbook that genuinely reflects the questions staff actually have is more useful than one written purely from a management perspective.

Linking the review to career progression

Where a staff member expresses interest in progressing to a more senior role, this is discussed as part of
the Annual Performance and Development Review and reflected in the personal development plan,
identifying the specific training or experience that would support that progression rather than leaving the
ambition undiscussed until a vacancy happens to arise.

New manager induction into supervision practice

A newly promoted line manager receives additional coaching on conducting supervision well before taking
on this responsibility for the first time, since giving good supervision is itself a skill that benefits from
support rather than being assumed to come automatically with a management title.

Supervision for an agency or bank worker

A regular agency or bank worker who covers shifts consistently at a site is also offered a lighter-touch
supervision conversation periodically with the shift lead, distinct from the more formal Alderbridge
employment relationship they have with their own agency, since a worker who is a familiar, regular
presence still benefits from the same kind of reflective conversation as a permanent colleague.

Group supervision alongside one-to-one sessions

Some sites also hold an occasional group supervision session covering a shared practice theme relevant
to the whole team, such as a recent change in a care approach, which complements but never replaces
the individual one-to-one supervision each staff member is separately entitled to.

Confidentiality of supervision content

What is discussed in supervision is treated as confidential between the staff member and their line
manager, save where it raises a safeguarding, conduct or safety concern that must be escalated under the
relevant separate policy, and staff are told clearly at the outset where that boundary sits so they can speak
openly within it.
